g.text: From mainframe source to reviewed requirements, business rules and a design to build from
Prerequisites → Sign in → Source → AWS Transform and Claude → Review → Reconcile → Design →
Assess mainframe source with AWS Transform and Claude, or with Claude only (--tools
claude, no AWS): with no options, a guided run that checks and sets up everything first;
the AWS resources stay until reframe teardown
Check and set up the prerequisites and the AWS sign-in, without starting a run
The run's stage, the job's plan steps, any waiting question and the next step
Show AWS's waiting question, or answer it
Continue a run that stopped; nothing with a receipt is repeated
Build the HTML report from the run's downloads again
The Claude assessment: assess the same snapshot with Claude's code-modernization plugin,
show it in the same business review, load its graph into the run's Neptune cluster, and
compare it with AWS Transform's results
The reconciliation: decide every rule the two assessments do not agree on (with Claude
only, every rule) against the source code, with evidence Reframe checks, then write
recommended requirements, one SME list and the reconciliation page; needs the run's
assessments done, and no AWS resources
Read the review downloads in a folder and show each reviewer's coverage, sign-offs and
where reviewers disagree; runs nothing, and the next reframe reconcile --context with
Write a run's reconciled results as one Excel workbook: domains, functions,
capabilities, requirements, business rules, decision tables, open questions and the SME
list, with the reviewers' marks; runs nothing
The design (pipeline 4): legacy and modern screens, journeys, the clickable prototype,
final specifications and the AI-DLC package, from the reconciled results; a round redoes
Build the page comparing AWS Transform's and Claude's results again
Optional: copy a run's reports, cleaned of the AWS account's identifiers, into a folder
others can open, upload the run's source, results and reports to your account's private
bucket, or publish the copy to a GitHub Pages site
The reports published to your AWS account: list them, open one with your AWS sign-in, or
List every AWS resource the run created, ask for consent, record it, then remove them
the home screen: your runs, the next step and a menu
a guided run: checks the prerequisites, the AWS
sign-in and the source, then starts
start straight away, with no questions
Claude only: no AWS account, nothing to tear down
where the latest run is, and what to do next
AWS's waiting question, in interactive mode
open the business review in the browser
the Claude assessment: the same snapshot, assessed
open the page comparing AWS Transform and Claude
the reconciled requirements and business rules as an
the design: screens, journeys, the prototype, final
upload the run's source, results and cleaned reports
list the published reports; reframe reports open
remove the AWS resources the run created
show program's version number and exit
